passage: Two hours before the application portal closed, Varun sat on a delayed train with his phone at fifteen per cent and one bar of signal, polishing his public profile. He had typed "visionary leader" and "award-winning" over a college quiz he had co-won. His sister Shreya called. "Why do you sound like a brochure?" Varun laughed, uneasy. He read it back and felt like an actor. He cut the puffed-up words and wrote what he had actually done: led a four-person project, co-won a state quiz. He kept the good photo. The cooking pictures stayed in the private account that only close friends could see. He submitted with a minute to spare.

qa.q: What did Shreya ask when she called?
qa.a: Shreya asked, Why do you sound like a brochure?

qa.q: How did Varun feel reading the profile back, and why?
qa.a: Like an actor; uneasy because the puffed-up words were not what Varun had actually done.

qa.q: Which choices kept the profile honest but still polished?
qa.a: Cutting the inflated words, stating what Varun had actually done and keeping the cooking pictures private.

qa.q: Why might Shreya have made the brochure remark?
qa.a: Shreya heard that the profile did not sound like Varun and joked gently to nudge honesty.

grounding: A young professional curates a public image, feels the strain of performing, and stays honest while keeping private space.

passage: In the Kolkata office lift, Yusuf overheard Arnab muttering a caption. "Led the whole campaign," it said. Arnab had actually built one of three parts. Every evening Arnab posted a polished update, and lately the effort felt like a second job: checking reactions before dinner and going to bed feeling flat. Yusuf said lightly, "You're better than your captions." Arnab thought about that all the way home. That night the caption became "Built the email part of a team campaign," and the post got fewer likes. Arnab felt lighter anyway. The weekend photos moved to a separate account with just a few close friends.

qa.q: How many parts of the campaign had Arnab actually built?
qa.a: Arnab had built one of three parts.

qa.q: How did Arnab feel about the daily posting, and what shows it?
qa.a: Arnab felt drained and weary; the effort felt like a second job and Arnab went to bed feeling flat.

qa.q: Which changes kept Arnab's image honest and protected privacy?
qa.a: Rewriting the caption to say exactly what Arnab did and moving weekend photos to a separate account for close friends.

qa.q: What might Yusuf have meant by You're better than your captions?
qa.a: That Arnab's real work was good enough and did not need exaggeration, said kindly and briefly.

grounding: A young professional curates a public image, feels the strain, and returns to honest captions and a private circle.
